authority.scope: provider-controlled pricing, entitlement, access-policy and authorization evidence
authority.rule: Provider evidence may classify provider-controlled facts, but it does not invent AI Premium Shop prices, availability, delivery promises, refunds or customer claims. Unknown provider facts remain unknown. Silence does not create vendor authorization.

review_method.scope: all providers represented by the 44 raw accessType=shared catalog records
review_method.rule: Use current first-party terms, legal, security or help-center sources. Apply an automatic publication block only when current evidence conflicts with the shared access represented by the raw record strongly enough to support that action. When evidence supports distinct invited/family/authorized-user access but does not evidence AI Premium Shop resale authorization, retain the owner-approved catalog row but never claim provider authorization and confirm the exact access arrangement before payment.

review_queue.priority: shared-access providers first, then highest-revenue and highest-traffic providers
review_queue.scope_result: All 37 providers represented by the current 44 raw shared-access records have a current first-party evidence classification or an explicit first-party-source access limitation recorded. Twenty-six provider-specific blocks are enforced. The two crawler-limited providers remain unknown on exact account-sharing language and therefore cannot be described as vendor-authorized.
reopen_when: a provider changes terms, account model, pricing or sharing rules
AI Premium Shop changes the exact fulfillment/access mechanism for a provider
a previously crawler-limited provider supplies accessible current legal text
owner or provider supplies written authorization that changes a current classification
review_queue.rule: Do not infer authorization from silence. A closed review means the current evidence state is classified, not that every provider authorizes resale or sharing.
